deep.reconstruction:
This page (sheet number '15', folio 21r) contains no mathematics. It is continuous prose from Section V of Riemann's manuscript on the mechanics of the ear, the text published posthumously by Henle in 1867 as 'Mechanik des Ohres' in the Zeitschrift für rationelle Medicin and reprinted in Riemann's Werke.

Context from the previous page: Riemann has stated conditions that the position of the middle-ear ossicles probably satisfies. The ossicles must stay in close contact, and no noticeably uneven tension may arise in the rim of the tympanic membrane or in the 'Paukenfell'. He now asks what means give and secure this correct position. His answer is pairs of opposing forces, which balance in the correct position and push the ossicle back if it is displaced. He says these forces must be sought in the two muscles, the joint capsules, the ligaments, the mucosal folds and the two membranes to which the ossicles are attached.

This page continues that discussion.
(i) When one looks for the causes of a given effect on the ossicles, often several mechanisms could produce it. This is especially so if the mucosal folds are included.
(ii) To pick the most probable mechanism, one would first need anatomical study of fresh specimens. This would give a rough judgement of the elasticity and tension of the ligaments, membranes and so on. Riemann states that this is impossible for him.
(iii) Alternative method: develop the consequences of each competing hypothesis carefully. The false ones should then lead to improbabilities and can be excluded. This is a hypothetico-deductive elimination strategy.
(iv) For the present investigation he distinguishes the 'listening' ear, adapted to precise hearing, from the non-listening ear. For certain questions he also distinguishes the newborn's ear from the adult's; the next page continues this.

The next page defines the listening state. The tensor tympani pulls the stapes footplate slightly against the labyrinth fluid. The fluid pressure then slightly exceeds the pressure in the tympanic cavity, so the solid parts whose contact must be secured are pressed lightly together.

In modern terms, the only implicit 'mechanics' is a stability criterion. The equilibrium position is one where the net generalized force vanishes, F(q0) = 0. It is stable when the restoring stiffness is positive, dF/dq < 0 at q0. This is my gloss; Riemann writes no formula.

results.what: Methodological statement: competing mechanical hypotheses for how the ossicles are held in position should be decided by deriving their consequences and eliminating those that lead to improbabilities, in place of unavailable measurements of ligament and membrane elasticity.
results.modern_name: Hypothetico-deductive elimination of hypotheses (Riemann's 'Mechanik des Ohres' methodology)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann, Mechanik des Ohres (published posthumously by Henle, 1867)

results.what: Distinction between the 'listening' ear (adapted to precise hearing, with slight tensor-tympani preload) and the non-listening ear, and between the newborn and adult ear.
results.modern_name: Accommodation/adaptation of the middle ear by the tensor tympani (preload of the ossicular chain)
results.usually_credited_to: Discussed in 19th-century otology (Helmholtz, Politzer, etc.); this formulation is in Riemann's published 'Mechanik des Ohres'

deep.surprise_reason: Purely discursive, methodological prose with no mathematics. The text corresponds to Riemann's posthumously published 'Mechanik des Ohres' (Henle 1867, in the Werke), so nothing here is new or unattributed.
transcription_corrections: The page carries the sheet number '15' at top right and the pencil folio number '21'; the machine transcription omits both.
'Häute zz.' is most likely the Kurrent abbreviation for 'etc.' (often written 'zc.' or '&c.'), i.e. 'Bänder, Häute etc.'.
'Gehörknöchelchen' in line 3 has an overwritten or corrected stroke above it in the image; the reading itself is correct.
The inserted comma after 'adaptirten' ({+,+}) is correctly shown as an interlinear addition; the remaining readings ('excludiren', 'Unwahrscheinlichkeiten', 'Consequenzen') agree with the image.
